h: Kit, timings and a few sneaky tips
p: Turning up prepared makes all the difference at an adventure park like this. Dress everyone in comfy sportswear that's easy to move in, without zips, buckles or belts that might snag. Leave jewellery and anything in pockets in a locker or the car, and tie back long hair. Grip socks are normally bought on your first visit, and most places let you reuse them, so keep hold of them for next time.

Get there ten or fifteen minutes before your slot. Between checking in, signing waivers and wrestling small feet into socks, it all takes longer than you'd think, and you'll want to be first through the door when your session starts. Listen to the safety briefing too: one person per trampoline and no piling on top of each other are the rules that keep a fun hour from ending in tears.

Bring a water bottle. Bouncing and climbing are much more tiring than they look, and kids will push themselves until they suddenly flop. Building in a couple of short breaks keeps tempers sweet and gets more out of the session.

For parties, book well ahead, especially for weekends, and check exactly what's included in the package so there are no surprises on the day. For younger children, look out for dedicated toddler or early-years sessions, which are usually calmer and far less intimidating.

Once everyone's worn out, Gateshead has some gentler options. Saltwell Park is a lovely Victorian park with a lake, gardens and play areas, perfect for a picnic. Or stroll down to the Quayside and walk across the Gateshead Millennium Bridge for a wander on the Newcastle side of the Tyne.
